title: Open normal subgroups containing inertia have unramified finite fixed fields
statement: Let $A$ be an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with fraction field $K$, and choose a separable closure $\Omega/K$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$ with its Krull topology. Let $C$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For each prime $\mathfrak r\subset C$, put $I_{\mathfrak r}=\{g\in G:g\mathfrak r=\mathfrak r,\ g|_{\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak r)}=1\}$. Let $U\subseteq G$ be an open normal subgroup such that $I_{\mathfrak r}\subseteq U$ for every prime $\mathfrak r$ of $C$. Define $L=\Omega^U=\{b\in\Omega:ub=b\text{ for every }u\in U\}$ and let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$. Then $L/K$ is finite Galois, meaning finite-dimensional, separable and normal, and $U=\operatorname{Aut}_L(\Omega)$. Every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ is the contraction of a prime $\mathfrak r\subset C$, and its inertia subgroup $\{h\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(L):h\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q,\ h|_{\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)}=1\}$ is trivial. No Noetherian hypothesis or finiteness of either integral closure is assumed.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois], $\Omega/K$ is Galois. Apply [lem-exc-etale-open-subgroup-fixed-field-galois] to the open subgroup $U$: its fixed field $L$ is finite-dimensional and separable over $K$, and its pointwise fixing subgroup in $G$ equals $U$. In particular $U=\operatorname{Aut}_L(\Omega)$. Since $U$ is normal, [lem-dl-a1-normal-fixing-subgroup-galois] applied to $K\subseteq L\subseteq\Omega$ shows that $L/K$ is Galois, hence normal as well as separable. Together these give precisely the finite Galois assertion.

source.place: Tag 0BML, theorem-inifinite-galois-theory, finite/open and normal/Galois clauses; used in Tag 0BTD second proof paragraph.

proof.text: Use the inclusions $A\subseteq B\subseteq C\subseteq\Omega$. Indeed an element of $B$ is integral over $A$, and remains so in $\Omega$, hence lies in $C$. Every $c\in C$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$; the same polynomial, with coefficients viewed in $B$, proves that $c$ is integral over $B$. Thus $B\hookrightarrow C$ is injective and integral. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] to obtain, for each prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$, a prime $\mathfrak r\subset C$ contracting to $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 00GQ, lemma-integral-overring-surjective; applied to the integral-closure inclusion in Tag 0BTD second proof paragraph.

proof.text: Fix such $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak r$. In the tower $\Omega/L/K$, both extensions over $K$ are Galois by step 1, and $A$ is a normal domain by hypothesis. Apply [lem-dl-a1-inertia-restriction-surjective] with $M=\Omega$ and these integral closures and primes: restriction surjects $I_{\mathfrak r}\to I_{\mathfrak q}$. For $h\in I_{\mathfrak q}$ choose a lift $g\in I_{\mathfrak r}$. The hypothesis gives $g\in U$, and the definition of $L=\Omega^U$ gives $g(b)=b$ for all $b\in L$. Consequently $h=g|_L=1$. Thus $I_{\mathfrak q}=\{1\}$ for every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$. No step used Noetherianity or finite generation of an integral closure.
